neighbours.label: text about the sun, stars and the earth's seasons and winds: fires on the function word that follows a physical-process verb there (cool over, once per, affected by, blows from)
fire: Red giants swell over millions of years until they swallow their inner planets.
The Moon circles the Earth about once per month, which produces the tides.
Young stars are often surrounded by discs of gas and dust.
The Sun rotates on its axis roughly every twenty-five days at the equator.
During the dry season the trade winds blow from the northeast across the islands.
Neutron stars spin down over time as they radiate away their energy.
The orbit of Mars is strongly influenced by the gravity of Jupiter.
Sunspots appear in cycles of about eleven years on the surface of the Sun.
quiet: Old towns swell over many years until they swallow the nearby villages.
The inspector visits the factory about once per month, which annoys the staff.
Young actors are often surrounded by agents and reporters.
The carousel rotates on its axle roughly every twenty-five seconds at full speed.
During the dry season the cattle are moved from the northeast across the plains.
Old machines slow down over time as their bearings wear away.
The price of wheat is strongly influenced by the cost of fuel.
Weeds appear in patches of about eleven metres on the edge of the field.

notes: Card: all top examples are astronomy or seasonal weather (sun sheds its outer layers, white dwarfs cool over time, Earth around the sun one time per year, wind blows from the southeast), peaking on ' of', ' the', ' to', ' its', ' over', ' per', ' by'. Probe: white dwarfs cool over time 1.04, once per year 0.88, blows from 0.81, affected by rotation 0.59, sun sheds 0.32; same frames about a snake or a bus 0.02. The - pole (max 232) is the return of the sun after the winter solstice, so the fire items avoid solstices and lengthening days.
